breaking_news.headline: How personal data is being used to control what customers see and pay
breaking_news.summary: NPR's Joel Rose speaks with Lindsay Owens, president of the economic think tank Groundwork Collaborative, about how companies using data to transform the products and prices customers see.

breaking_news.headline: 2 Americans win Nobel Prize in economics for work on boom-bust cycles
breaking_news.summary: Two Americans have won the Nobel Prize in economics for their work on how to smooth boom-and-bust cycles to limit unemployment and inflation.

breaking_news.headline: Farmers say they'll take the relief of Trump's EO — but they're still hurting
breaking_news.summary: President Trump says his Monday executive order temporarily suspending federal taxes on diesel will be a big relief for farmers. Some farmers call it a campaign ploy with marginal impact.

breaking_news.headline: What ice cream has to do with this year's Nobel Prize in economics
breaking_news.summary: Prices can get sticky. That helps explain why recessions hurt so much — and what policymakers can do about them.

breaking_news.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico prevail against White House — for now
breaking_news.summary: A federal judge ruled late Tuesday that President Trump cannot ban news organizations from covering him at the White House because he does not like the nature of their coverage - at least, not until the matter goes to a formal trial.

breaking_news.headline: VIDEO: The skincare sample is free. What happens next can cost thousands
breaking_news.summary: For years, customers have complained of aggressive sales tactics and charges at mall skincare stores. NPR investigated the business that connects many of them.

breaking_news.headline: The skincare scheme that led to consumer complaints, lawsuits and a federal investigation
breaking_news.summary: Free samples, high-pressure pitches and $50,000 bills: An NPR investigation reveals how a network of mall skincare stores systematically targeted older adults and people with disabilities across the U.S.

breaking_news.headline: Inflation sizzled in September — and Social Security benefits will get a boost
breaking_news.summary: Consumer prices in September jumped 3.7% from a year ago.  The Social Security Administration said benefits will increase next year to help keep pace with the rising cost of living.

breaking_news.headline: Hundreds of thousands of workers on strike across Republic of Ireland
breaking_news.summary: It comes amidst an an ongoing pay dispute between public sector workers and the Irish government.

breaking_news.headline: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
breaking_news.summary: It follows the death last week of a man who had arrived in Kenya after travelling from DR Congo.

breaking_news.headline: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
breaking_news.summary: All of the spots are in South Australia, reportedly because the state government paid for incognito inspectors to visit.

breaking_news.headline: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
breaking_news.summary: Four years after the attacks, Serhii Kuznetsov appears in court accused of a plot to destroy Russia's gas pipelines to Germany.

breaking_news.headline: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
breaking_news.summary: The 71-year-old Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the 90-minute procedure on Tuesday.

breaking_news.headline: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
breaking_news.summary: Elon Musk's system allows Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and effectively guide drones to Russian targets.

breaking_news.headline: Civil servant faked illness with make-up to juggle five jobs, court hears
breaking_news.summary: Kashim Chowdhury is accused of fraudulently juggling multiple government jobs while working from home.

breaking_news.headline: US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices
breaking_news.summary: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September, driving by higher motor fuel costs.

breaking_news.headline: How long will humans be needed for translation?
breaking_news.summary: AI dominates the translation business, but for high-stakes work, humans are still needed.

breaking_news.headline: Driving test waits fall to two-year low - but still average 20 weeks
breaking_news.summary: Learner drivers in September had to wait an average of 19.7 weeks, or around five months, for a practical test.

breaking_news.headline: Faisal Islam: What surprise praise for UK economy tells us about the Budget
breaking_news.summary: On three occasions in the past 24 hours, top IMF officials have praised UK plans to reduce its annual levels of borrowing.

breaking_news.headline: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer
breaking_news.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan had worked for the AI giant for more than a year before he was arrested by the FBI.
